title: Reference-Augmented Learning for Precise Tracking Policy of Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots
summary: Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots (TDCRs) pose significant control challenges due to their highly nonlinear, path-dependent dynamics and non-Markovian characteristics. Traditional Jacobian-based controllers often struggle with hysteresis-induced oscillations, while conventional learning-based approaches suffer from poor generalization to out-of-distribution trajectories. This paper proposes a reference-augmented offline learning framework for precise 6-DOF tracking control of TDCRs. By leveraging a differentiable RNN-based dynamics surrogate as a gradient bridge, we optimize a control policy through an augmented reference distribution. This multi-scale augmentation scheme incorporates stochastic bias, harmonic perturbations, and random walks, forcing the policy to internalize diverse tracking error recovery mechanisms without additional hardware interaction. Experimental results on a three-section TDCR platform demonstrate that the proposed policy achieves a 50.9\% reduction in average position error compared to non-augmented baselines and significantly outperforms Jacobian-based methods in both precision and stability across various speeds.
tldr: This paper proposes a reference‑augmented offline learning framework for precise 6‑DOF tracking of tendon‑driven continuum robots, employing a differentiable RNN‑based dynamics surrogate and multi‑scale augmentation (stochastic bias, harmonic perturbations, random walks). Experiments demonstrate a 50.9% reduction in average position error versus non‑augmented baselines and superior performance over Jacobian‑based controllers.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种参考增强的离线学习框架，用于实现腱驱动连续体机器人的6自由度精确跟踪。该方法利用可微分的RNN动力学代理模型和多尺度增强（随机偏置、谐波扰动、随机游走），实验表明平均位置误差比基线降低50.9%，且在精度和稳定性上优于雅可比控制器。
summary_zh: 肌腱驱动连续体机器人（TDCRs）由于其高度非线性的、路径依赖的动力学特性以及非马尔可夫特性，带来了重大的控制挑战。传统基于雅可比矩阵的控制器通常难以应对滞后引起的振荡问题，而传统的基于学习的方法在推广到分布外轨迹时表现较差。本文提出了一种参考增强离线学习框架，用于实现TDCRs的精确6自由度跟踪控制。通过利用可微循环神经网络（RNN）动力学代理模型作为梯度桥，我们通过增强参考分布来优化控制策略。这种多尺度增强方案结合了随机偏置、谐波扰动和随机游走，迫使策略内化多种跟踪误差恢复机制，而无需额外的硬件交互。在三段式TDCR平台上的实验结果表明，与非增强基线相比，所提出的策略将平均位置误差降低了50.9%，并在各种速度下在精度和稳定性方面均显著优于基于雅可比矩阵的方法。

title: Learning-Based Dynamics Modeling and Robust Control for Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots
summary: Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots (TDCRs) pose significant modeling and control challenges due to complex nonlinearities, such as frictional hysteresis and transmission compliance. This paper proposes a differentiable learning framework that integrates high-fidelity dynamics modeling with robust neural control. We develop a GRU-based dynamics model featuring bidirectional multi-channel connectivity and residual prediction to effectively suppress compounding errors during long-horizon auto-regressive prediction. By treating this model as a gradient bridge, an end-to-end neural control policy is optimized through backpropagation, allowing it to implicitly internalize compensation for intricate nonlinearities. Experimental validation on a physical three-section TDCR demonstrates that our framework achieves accurate tracking and superior robustness against unseen payloads, outperforming Jacobian-based methods by eliminating self-excited oscillations.
tldr: This paper introduces a differentiable learning framework that combines a GRU‑based dynamics model with residual prediction and an end‑to‑end neural control policy to address the nonlinear modeling and control challenges of tendon‑driven continuum robots, demonstrating accurate tracking and robust performance against unseen payloads on a physical three‑section TDCR.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种可微分的学习框架，将基于GRU的高保真动力学模型与残差预测及端到端神经控制策略相结合，以解决腱驱动连续体机器人的非线性建模与控制难题，并在三段式TDCR上展示了精确跟踪和對未知负载的强鲁棒性。
summary_zh: 肌腱驱动连续体机器人（TDCRs）由于复杂的非线性特性（如摩擦滞后和传动柔顺性），在建模与控制方面面临重大挑战。本文提出了一种可微学习框架，将高保真动力学建模与鲁棒神经控制相结合。我们开发了一种基于GRU的动力学模型，采用双向多通道连接和残差预测技术，以有效抑制长时域自回归预测过程中的累积误差。通过将该模型作为梯度桥接器，利用反向传播优化端到端神经控制策略，使其能够隐式内化对复杂非线性特性的补偿能力。在物理三段式TDCR上的实验验证表明，我们的框架实现了精确跟踪，并对未知负载展现出卓越的鲁棒性，优于基于雅可比矩阵的方法，消除了自激振荡现象。

title: SAMe: A Semantic Anatomy Mapping Engine for Robotic Ultrasound
summary: Robotic ultrasound has advanced local image-driven control, contact regulation, and view optimization, yet current systems lack the anatomical understanding needed to determine what to scan, where to begin, and how to adapt to individual patient anatomy. These gaps make systems still reliant on expert intervention to initiate scanning. Here we present SAMe, a semantic anatomy mapping engine that provides robotic ultrasound with an explicit anatomical prior layer. SAMe addresses scan initiation as a target-to-anatomy-to-action process: it grounds under-specified clinical complaints into structured target organs, instantiates a patient-specific anatomical representation for the grounded targets from a single external body image, and translates this representation into control-facing 6-DoF probe initialization states without any additional registration using preoperative CT or MRI. The anatomical representation maintained by SAMe is explicit, lightweight (single-organ inference in 0.08s), and compatible with downstream control by design. Across semantic grounding, anatomical instantiation, and real-robot evaluation, SAMe shows strong performance across the full initialization pipeline. In real-robot experiments, SAMe achieved overall organ-hit rates of 97.3% for liver initialization and 81.7% for kidney initialization across the evaluated target sets. Even when restricted to the centroid target, SAMe outperformed the surface-heuristic baseline for both liver and kidney initialization. These results establish an explicit anatomical prior layer that addresses scan initialization and is designed to support broader downstream autonomous scanning pipelines, providing the anatomical foundation for complaint-driven, anatomically informed robotic ultrasonography.
tldr: The paper introduces SAMe, a semantic anatomy mapping engine that infers patient‑specific organ locations from a single external body image to generate 6‑DoF probe initialization states for robotic ultrasound, achieving 97.3% liver and 81.7% kidney hit rates in real‑robot experiments.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了SAMe，一种语义解剖映射引擎，通过单张外部人体图像推断患者特定的器官位置，生成机器人超声探头的6自由度初始化状态，在实际机器人实验中实现了肝脏97.3%和肾脏81.7%的命中率。
summary_zh: 机器人超声技术在局部图像驱动控制、接触调节和视图优化方面取得了进展，然而当前系统仍缺乏必要的解剖学理解，无法确定扫描内容、起始位置以及如何适应个体患者解剖结构。这些差距使得系统仍然依赖专家干预来启动扫描。在此，我们提出SAMe，一种为机器人超声提供显式解剖先验层的语义解剖映射引擎。SAMe将扫描初始化作为一个目标-解剖-动作过程来处理：它将未明确指定的临床主诉锚定到结构化目标器官，从单张外部本体图像为锚定的目标实例化患者特异性解剖表示，并将该表示转换为面向控制的6自由度探头初始化状态，无需使用术前CT或MRI进行任何额外配准。SAMe维护的解剖表示具有显式、轻量级（单器官推理仅需0.08秒）的特点，并从设计上兼容下游控制。在语义锚定、解剖实例化和真实机器人评估中，SAMe在整个初始化流程中表现出色。在真实机器人实验中，SAMe在肝脏初始化中达到了97.3%的总体器官命中率，在肾脏初始化中达到了81.7%的总体器官命中率，跨越了所有评估的目标点。即使仅限于质心目标，SAMe在肝脏和肾脏初始化方面的表现也优于表面启发式基准。这些结果确立了一个显式解剖先验层，该先验层解决了扫描初始化问题，并旨在支持更广泛的下游自主扫描流程，为主诉驱动、解剖信息引导的机器人超声检查提供了解剖学基础。

title: Image Compression with Bubble-Aware Frame Rate Adaptation for Energy-Efficient Video Capsule Endoscopy
summary: Video Capsule Endoscopy (VCE) is a promising method for improving the medical examination of the small intestine in the gastrointestinal tract. A key challenge is their limited size, resulting in a short battery lifetime which conflicts with high energy consumption for image capturing and transmission to an on-body device. Thus, we propose an image compression pipeline that substantially reduces the transmitted data while preserving diagnostic image quality. Furthermore, we exploit characteristics of the compression process to identify frames with low diagnostic value mainly caused by bubbles, without requiring additional image analysis. For low-visibility frames, a dynamic bubble-aware frame rate adaptation strategy reduces image acquisition and transmission during these phases while preserving sensitivity to potential anomalies. The proposed compression and frame rate adaptation are evaluated on a RISC-V platform using the Kvasir-Capsule and Galar datasets. The compression method achieves a compression ratio of 5.748 (82.6%) at a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 40.3 dB, indicating negligible loss of visual quality. The compression accomplished a mean energy reduction of the whole system by 20.58%. Additionally, the proposed bubble-aware frame rate adaptation reduced the energy consumption by up to 40%. These results demonstrate the potential of our method to increase the applicability of VCE.
tldr: The paper proposes an image‑compression pipeline that exploits compression characteristics to detect low‑diagnostic‑value frames (mainly bubbles) and applies a dynamic bubble‑aware frame‑rate adaptation, achieving a 5.7× compression ratio and up to 40% energy reduction for video capsule endoscopy.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出一种利用压缩特征识别低诊断价值帧（主要是气泡）并实现动态气泡感知的帧率适配的图像压缩方案，在视频胶囊内镜中实现了约5.7倍的压缩比和最高40%的能耗降低。
summary_zh: 视频胶囊内镜（VCE）是一种有望改善胃肠道小肠医学检查的方法。其中的一个关键挑战在于其尺寸受限，导致电池续航时间短，而这与图像采集和向体表设备传输的高能耗之间存在矛盾。因此，我们提出了一种图像压缩流程，该流程在保持诊断图像质量的同时大幅减少传输数据量。此外，我们利用压缩过程的特性来识别诊断价值较低的帧，这些帧主要由气泡引起，无需额外的图像分析即可实现。对于低能见度帧，我们采用动态气泡感知帧率自适应策略，在这些阶段减少图像采集和传输，同时保持对潜在异常的敏感性。我们在RISC-V平台上使用Kvasir-Capsule和Galar数据集对所提出的压缩和帧率自适应方法进行了评估。压缩方法在峰值信噪比为40.3 dB时达到了5.748的压缩比（82.6%），表明视觉质量损失可忽略不计。压缩使整个系统的平均能耗降低了20.58%。此外，所提出的气泡感知帧率自适应将能耗降低了高达40%。这些结果表明，我们的方法有望提高VCE的适用性。
